title: Do “moderate” drinkers have reduced mortality risk? A systematic review and meta-analysis of alcohol consumption and all-cause mortality
authors: Stockwell T, Zhao J, Panwar S, Roemer A, Naimi T, Chikritzhs T
journal: Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs
population: 87 prospective studies of alcohol consumption and all-cause mortality, 367,103 deaths
funder: This study was funded by National Institutes of Health Award # 1RO1AAO19939-02.
authorConflicts: No conflict-of-interest statement in the PMC full text.
result: Of 87 studies, 65 included former drinkers and 50 occasional drinkers in the abstainer reference group; 13 were free of both biases. Without adjustment, low-volume drinkers (1.3 to 24.9 g ethanol per day) had RR 0.86 (95% CI 0.83 to 0.90) and former drinkers RR 1.22 (1.14 to 1.31) against abstainers. After adjustment for abstainer biases and study characteristics, low-volume drinkers had RR 0.97 (0.88 to 1.07).
